verification.spec: Assert the simulator's configured horizon >=100000 slots and that final logged timestamp reaches at least 10^5 for the unstable run, and includes the window [96500, 100000] for the stable run.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that produces four log-scale plots analogous to Figure 8: for each policy (unstable Up, stable Down), one plot of #requests vs time and one plot of #tokens vs time, each showing curves for agent 1 and agent 2 separately.

verification.spec: Run the plotting script; assert that four PNG/PDF files are produced with log-scale y-axes, each containing two labeled curves (agent 1 and agent 2), corresponding to (unstable-requests, unstable-tokens, stable-requests, stable-tokens).

sub_tasks.requirements: The measured simulation outputs match the qualitative and quantitative claims about instability under the specified priority and stability under its reversal.

Under the unstable policy (Figure 8 Up), the total number of tokens across both agents grows without bound over time, reaching on the order of 10^6-10^7 tokens by time ~10^5, consistent with Figure 8 [Up] right panel.

verification.spec: Run the unstable-policy simulation for 10^5 slots; measure the total tokens summed across both agents at t=10^5. Assert value falls in [10^6, 10^7].

sub_tasks.requirements: Under the unstable policy (Figure 8 Up), the total number of outstanding requests at both agents grows over time to on the order of 10^4-10^5 by time ~10^5, consistent with Figure 8 [Up] left panel.

verification.spec: Run the unstable-policy simulation for 10^5 slots; measure the total outstanding requests summed across both agents at t=10^5. Assert value is in [10^4, 10^5].

sub_tasks.requirements: Under the reversed (stable) policy (Figure 8 Down), the total number of tokens at each agent remains bounded over the observation window [96500, 100000], staying on the order of at most ~10^4 as in Figure 8 [Down] right panel.

verification.spec: Run the reversed (stable) policy simulation through t=10^5 slots; compute max token count at each agent over the window [96500, 100000]. Assert max <= ~10^4 for both agents.

sub_tasks.requirements: Under the reversed (stable) policy (Figure 8 Down), the total number of outstanding requests at each agent remains bounded (on the order of at most ~10^2) over the window [96500, 100000], consistent with Figure 8 [Down] left panel.

verification.spec: Run the reversed (stable) policy simulation through t=10^5; compute max outstanding requests at each agent over the window [96500, 100000]. Assert max <= ~10^2 for both agents.

sub_tasks.requirements: The experiment confirms that instability occurs under the specified work-conserving priority policy even though ρ = 0.9 < 1, demonstrating that not all work-conserving policies stabilize the RS-type network.

verification.spec: Verify (i) that the RS-network load ρ computed from the specified arrival rate and mean token sizes equals 0.9 (<1), and (ii) that under the unstable work-conserving priority policy, the token count time-series exhibits strictly increasing trend (linear regression slope > 0 on log-scale samples across t in [10^3, 10^5]).

depends_on: AI-Agent Workload: Two-Type Single Engine and Fork-Join Network

sub_tasks.requirements: Reproduce Figure 9: end-to-end latency and TTFT CCDFs for Sarathi-Serve on CodeLlama-34B under scaled production conversation traces across token budgets 128, 512, and 1024, matching the reported median values (75.97, 94.23, 101.30 for E2E and 115.01, 113.37, 178.65 for prefill).
Experimental configuration matches the paper's Figure 9 setup: CodeLlama-34B on Sarathi-Serve with scaled production conversation traces and three token-budget sweeps.

verification.spec: Launch Sarathi-Serve with model=codellama/CodeLlama-34b-hf. Assert model loads successfully, and profile a few batches to verify measured batch time approximates c=46.71 + 0.289*(x-128)+ ms within 20%.

verification.spec: Inspect the experiment driver/config: assert it iterates exactly over token_budget ∈ {128, 512, 1024} and produces three separate result artifacts, with other parameters identical across runs (diff configs to confirm).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to load a production conversation trace (real prompt/response length distribution) and drive requests into the serving engine according to the trace's arrival timestamps.

verification.spec: Verify the trace loader: given a production conversation trace file, the client sends requests with the same arrival timestamps (or scaled version) and with prompt/response token counts drawn from the trace. Compare loaded distribution stats to trace file stats.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to scale the production conversation trace's arrival rate to the high-arrival-rate regime used in Figure 9 so that the engine operates near (but under) its stability boundary given by load condition (2.7).

verification.spec: Verify the arrival rate scaling routine: given trace mean token load and system capacity b/t_b, the produced arrival rate satisfies (m_p + m_d) * λ < b/t_b (per condition 2.7) and reaches at least 80% of that bound. Log the computed ρ.

sub_tasks.requirements: Instrumentation that records per-request TTFT and end-to-end latency and produces CCDF curves matching Figure 9's axes.
Code has been implemented to record TTFT (time from request arrival to first generated token) for every request across the run.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to compute the complementary CDF (CCDF) of the recorded latency samples for both E2E and prefill (TTFT) metrics per token-budget setting.

verification.spec: Feed synthetic latency samples into the CCDF computation routine and assert output equals 1 - empirical_CDF at each sample point. Run separately for both E2E and TTFT arrays and for all three token budgets.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to extract the median (50th percentile) of the E2E and TTFT distributions for each of the three token budgets and report them in the same ms units as Figure 9.

verification.spec: Inspect the reporting output: assert it contains a table with 3 rows (one per token budget) and columns for median E2E (ms) and median TTFT (ms), each numeric.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to plot CCDF curves on log-x axes (E2E and prefill separately) with one curve per token budget, reproducing the layout of Figure 9.

verification.spec: Run the plotting script; assert two output figures are produced (E2E and prefill), each with log-scaled x-axis and three labeled curves corresponding to token budgets 128, 512, 1024.

verification.spec: Compare median TTFTs across Sarathi-Serve with token budgets 128 and 512 on CodeLlama-34B. Assert that median_TTFT(512) <= median_TTFT(128), reflecting overhead of overly-small budgets from repeated cross-attention.

sub_tasks.requirements: The extended batch-processing-time model incorporating attention computation (Appendix A.1) and the piecewise KV-cache overhead model (Appendix A.2) are implemented as described.
The extended batch processing time model with attention computation (Appendix A.1) is implemented.

Code has been implemented that defines a batch processing time function for batch n as t_{b'} = c + a * max(b' - b_0, 0) + alpha * sum_{i in batch}(delta_i^p * (bar_P_i(n) + bar_D_i(n))) + beta * sum_{i in batch}(delta_i^d * (bar_P_i(n) + bar_D_i(n))), matching the formula in Appendix A.1.

verification.spec: Import the batch-processing-time function. Construct synthetic batches with known (delta_i^p, delta_i^d, bar_P_i, bar_D_i) and check the returned time equals c + a*max(b'-b_0,0) + alpha*sum(delta_i^p*(bar_P_i+bar_D_i)) + beta*sum(delta_i^d*(bar_P_i+bar_D_i)) for several parameter settings.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that maintains, per request i and per batch n, the cumulative counts bar_P_i(n) of processed prompt tokens and bar_D_i(n) of decoded tokens up to and including batch n, and exposes these state variables to the batch-time model.

verification.spec: Instantiate the engine state, simulate a sequence of batches with known delta_i^p/delta_i^d per request, and after each batch assert that bar_P_i(n) equals cumulative sum of prefill tokens processed and bar_D_i(n) equals cumulative sum of decode tokens for request i. Assert these values are readable and passed to the batch-time model.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that treats the attention-cost coefficients alpha and beta as configurable model/hardware-dependent constants, loadable from a configuration for at least the CodeLlama-34B and Llama-3-70B configurations used in the paper.

verification.spec: Load a configuration file (or config object) for CodeLlama-34B and Llama-3-70B and assert that alpha and beta appear as configurable numeric fields per model. Assert changing them in the config changes the batch-time function output.

sub_tasks.requirements: When alpha = beta = 0, the extended batch-processing-time function reduces exactly to the short-context piecewise-linear form t_{b'} = c + a * max(b' - b_0, 0), verified by a unit test comparing outputs on a set of representative token loads b'.

verification.spec: Set alpha=beta=0 in the extended batch-time function and evaluate on token loads b' in {32,64,128,256,512,1024}. Assert output equals c + a*max(b'-b_0,0) exactly (within float tolerance) for known (c,a,b_0).

sub_tasks.requirements: A unit test verifies that with nonzero alpha and beta, the batch-processing-time output increases monotonically as the cumulative context lengths bar_P_i + bar_D_i of tokens included in the batch grow (holding token load b' fixed), reflecting the non-linear long-context behavior described in Appendix A.1.

verification.spec: Fix batch token load b' and delta assignments. Vary the cumulative context lengths (bar_P_i + bar_D_i) upward across trials with alpha,beta > 0. Assert batch time is monotonically non-decreasing (strictly increasing when any token in the batch has increased context).

sub_tasks.requirements: The piecewise KV-cache memory-overhead model (Appendix A.2) is implemented.
Code has been implemented that computes, per request i, the number x_i of KV tokens exceeding the configured memory limit, given the request's current KV footprint and the engine's KV-cache capacity.

verification.spec: Configure engine with a KV-cache capacity C. For requests with varying KV footprints, invoke the computation of x_i and assert x_i = max(0, footprint_i - allocated_i) matches the formula in Appendix A.2 across several test cases.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that defines the piecewise overhead function o(x_i) with two regimes (e.g., swap/offload regime a_1 * x_i + b_1 and recomputation regime a_2 * x_i + b_2) as specified in Appendix A.2, and selects between them according to the configured KV policy.

verification.spec: Import overhead function o(x_i). Set KV policy to 'swap' and check o(x_i) = a_1*x_i + b_1 for x_i>0. Switch policy to 'recompute' and check o(x_i) = a_2*x_i + b_2. Verify both branches selectable via a config flag.

sub_tasks.requirements: The coefficients (a_1, a_2, b_1, b_2) of the piecewise overhead model are exposed as configuration parameters tied to system-level quantities (CPU-GPU bandwidth, chunk size, hidden dimension, and other model configuration), rather than hard-coded.

verification.spec: Inspect the configuration schema for the overhead model. Assert that a_1,a_2,b_1,b_2 are parameterized in terms of CPU-GPU bandwidth, chunk size, hidden dimension, etc. (not hard-coded constants). Programmatically vary bandwidth in config and assert a_1/b_1 change accordingly.

sub_tasks.requirements: A unit test verifies that o(x_i) = 0 when x_i <= 0 (i.e., the request fits in KV cache), and that o(x_i) is non-negative and piecewise-linear in x_i for x_i > 0 under each of the two policy branches.

verification.spec: Call o(x_i) at x_i in {-10, 0}: assert result == 0. Call at x_i in {1,10,100,1000} under both swap and recompute policies: assert result >= 0 and slope (o(x2)-o(x1))/(x2-x1) is constant within each branch (piecewise-linear).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that composes the KV-overhead o(x_i) additively into the extended batch processing time function from Appendix A.1, so the total per-batch time reflects both attention cost and KV-memory overhead when both are enabled.

verification.spec: Enable both attention model (A.1) and KV overhead (A.2). For a batch with known (delta, bar_P, bar_D) and requests exceeding KV capacity, assert total_time == A1_time + sum_i o(x_i) matches expected additive composition, and that disabling KV overhead recovers A.1-only time.

sub_tasks.requirements: The fluid model equations (C.10)-(C.17), definitions of stability/weak instability, Proposition 2, and the fluid-limit construction (Lemma 1-3) proving each limit is a fluid solution are reproduced.
The bookkeeping quantities and dynamic equations of the LLM engine (Appendix C.1) that underlie the fluid model are implemented.

Code has been implemented that maintains the per-slot quantities Z_p(n), Z_d(n), W_p(n), W_d(n), B_p(n), B_d(n), F_p(n), F_d(n), E(n), and V_p(N), V_d(N) as defined in Appendix C.1 for a single LLM engine, updating them each iteration from arrivals, batching decisions, and completions.

verification.spec: Run a short simulation of a single LLM engine under a (K_p,K_d)-FCFS work-conserving policy. After each time slot n, assert the simulator exposes Z_p(n), Z_d(n), W_p(n), W_d(n), B_p(n), B_d(n), F_p(n), F_d(n), E(n), V_p(N), V_d(N) as documented, and that Z_p(n)+Z_d(n) matches the number of pending tokens computed independently.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that enforces the flow-conservation identities of Appendix C.1 (linking Z_f, W_f, B_f, F_f, V_f, and E) so that at every simulated time slot the accounting equations hold exactly under any (K_p, K_d)-FCFS scheduling algorithm.

verification.spec: Simulate several time slots under randomized arrivals and a (K_p,K_d)-FCFS policy. After each slot, verify each conservation identity from Appendix C.1 (linking Z_f, W_f, B_f, F_f, V_f, E) holds exactly (equality) at every n.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that realizes the (K_p, K_d)-FCFS key relationship (Eq. C.9 in Appendix C.1) governing which oldest requests contribute prefill/decode tokens to a batch, matching the same structural form as Eq. (6.51) of Dai & Harrison (2020).

verification.spec: Configure K_p and K_d. Simulate arrivals so there are more than K_f pending requests in phase f. Assert that at each batching decision only the K_f oldest requests in phase f contribute tokens to the batch, matching the structural form of Eq. (C.9)/Eq. (6.51) of Dai & Harrison.

sub_tasks.requirements: The fluid model equations (C.10)-(C.17), together with the notion of regular points and work-conserving fluid solutions, are encoded as verifiable properties.

Code has been implemented that represents fluid-model equations (C.10)-(C.11) relating Z_f(t), F_f(t), and arrival counts for phases f in {p, d}, and that can numerically check them for any candidate fluid trajectory.

verification.spec: Construct a fluid trajectory (Z_f, F_f, arrivals) as piecewise-linear functions on [0,T]. Call the checker; assert it returns True for trajectories satisfying (C.10)-(C.11) and False when Z_f or F_f is perturbed to violate the relation.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that enforces fluid-model equation (C.12): B_f(·) is Lipschitz with constant b/t_b, i.e. B_f(t)-B_f(s) ≤ (b/t_b)(t-s) for all 0≤s≤t and f∈{p,d}, and provides a checker function that verifies this on discrete samples of a fluid solution.

verification.spec: Provide sampled fluid trajectories of B_p and B_d. Call the Lipschitz checker; assert it returns True when (B_f(t)-B_f(s))/(t-s) <= b/t_b for all sample pairs and False when a violation is injected.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that encodes fluid-model equations (C.13) and (C.14) linking F_f(·), B_f(·), and W_f(·), and verifies Lipschitz continuity of the resulting F_f and W_f components.

verification.spec: Provide sampled fluid trajectories of F_f, B_f, W_f. Call the checker; assert equations (C.13) and (C.14) hold within numerical tolerance, and that F_f and W_f are certified Lipschitz. Introduce a violation and assert checker rejects.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that encodes the work-conserving fluid-model equation (C.17): at any regular point t with W_p(t)+W_d(t) > 0, the derivative sum \dot B_p(t)+\dot B_d(t) equals b/t_b, and provides a numerical test that this holds for fluid solutions produced under work-conserving (K_p,K_d)-FCFS algorithms.

verification.spec: Generate a fluid solution from a scaled simulation of a work-conserving (K_p,K_d)-FCFS policy. At each regular point where W_p(t)+W_d(t) > 0, numerically differentiate B_p+B_d and assert derivative equals b/t_b within tolerance.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that identifies regular points of a fluid solution (points where the vector-valued state function is differentiable) as defined in Definition 1, and exposes an API for querying derivatives at such points.

verification.spec: Given a piecewise-linear fluid trajectory, call the API to enumerate regular points and query derivatives. Assert non-differentiable kinks are excluded, and that the returned derivatives at interior linear segments match analytic slopes.

sub_tasks.requirements: The stability and weak-instability definitions (Definitions 3 and 4) and the workload Lyapunov function of Proposition 2 are implemented.

Code has been implemented that checks fluid-model stability per Definition 3: given any fluid solution with |Z(0)| = Z_p(0)+Z_d(0) ≤ 1, it verifies existence of a fixed δ > 0 such that Z(t)=0 for t≥δ.

verification.spec: Given a fluid solution with |Z(0)| <= 1 produced under load condition (2.7), call the stability checker. Assert it returns delta > 0 such that Z(t)=0 for all t >= delta on the sampled trajectory. Verify it rejects (returns no such delta) for an unstable trajectory (e.g., overloaded case).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that checks fluid-model weak instability per Definition 4: given any fluid solution starting from 0, it verifies existence of a fixed a > 0 with Z_p(a)+Z_d(a) ≠ 0.

verification.spec: Import the module implementing the weak-instability checker. Construct several fluid solutions starting from Z(0)=0: (i) one under overload with lambda*(m_p+m_d) > b/t_p, and (ii) one under underload with lambda*(m_p+m_d) < b/t_p. The checker must return True (there exists a>0 with Z_p(a)+Z_d(a) != 0) for case (i) and False for case (ii), matching Definition 4 in Appendix C.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that computes the workload Lyapunov function f(t) = m_p Z_p(t) + (m_p+m_d) Z_d(t) (Eq. C.19) used in the proof of Proposition 2, along with its almost-everywhere derivative on a fluid solution.

verification.spec: Import the Lyapunov-function module. On a supplied fluid trajectory (Z_p(t), Z_d(t)) with given m_p, m_d, verify that f(t) = m_p*Z_p(t) + (m_p+m_d)*Z_d(t) matches Eq. C.19 pointwise at sampled times, and that the numerical almost-everywhere derivative agrees with the analytical derivative (dot f = m_p*dot Z_p + (m_p+m_d)*dot Z_d) up to 1e-6 on regular points.

sub_tasks.requirements: Proposition 2 (fluid-model stability under load condition (C.1) and weak instability under overload (C.18)) is verified numerically on generated fluid solutions.

Code has been implemented that, given λ, m_p, m_d, b, t_p, and a work-conserving (K_p,K_d)-FCFS fluid solution satisfying load condition (C.1), computes \dot f(t) at regular points where f(t)>0 and verifies it equals λ(m_p+m_d) - b/t_p, which is strictly negative.

verification.spec: Simulate a work-conserving (K_p,K_d)-FCFS fluid solution with parameters lambda=1.0, m_p=1.0, m_d=1.0, b=4, t_p=1 (so b/t_p=4 and lambda*(m_p+m_d)=2, delta=2>0, load condition satisfied). At regular time points where f(t)>0, compute dot f(t) numerically and verify it equals lambda*(m_p+m_d) - b/t_p = -2.0 within tolerance.

sub_tasks.requirements: For a work-conserving fluid solution with |Z(0)|≤1 under load condition (C.1), the implementation numerically verifies Proposition 2(a) by showing f(t) reaches 0 no later than f(0)/δ with δ = b/t_p - λ(m_p+m_d), and Z(t)=0 thereafter.

verification.spec: Run a fluid-solution simulator with |Z(0)|<=1 under a work-conserving (K_p,K_d)-FCFS policy with lambda*(m_p+m_d) < b/t_p (delta = b/t_p - lambda*(m_p+m_d) > 0). Measure the first time T* at which f(t) reaches 0. Verify T* <= f(0)/delta and that Z_p(t)=Z_d(t)=0 for all t in [T*, T*+1].

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that, under overload condition (C.18) λ(m_p+m_d) > b/t_p, generates a fluid solution starting from 0 under an arbitrary scheduling algorithm and verifies that f(t) = (λ(m_p+m_d) - b/t_p)·t at regular points, so f(a)>0 (hence Z_p(a)+Z_d(a)≠0) for any a>0, matching Proposition 2(b).

verification.spec: Simulate a fluid solution starting from Z(0)=0 under overload (e.g. lambda=3, m_p=m_d=1, b=4, t_p=1 so lambda*(m_p+m_d)=6 > b/t_p=4) under an arbitrary scheduling algorithm. Verify at multiple regular times t that f(t) = (lambda*(m_p+m_d) - b/t_p)*t = 2t within tolerance, and that Z_p(a)+Z_d(a) > 0 for any a>0.

sub_tasks.requirements: The fluid-limit construction of Appendix C.3, including scaled processes and Lemmas 1-3 showing each limit is a fluid solution, is implemented and validated.

Code has been implemented that constructs the fluid-scaled processes \bar B_f^x, \bar E^x, \bar F_f^x, \bar W_f^x, \bar Z_f^x from a stochastic simulation of the LLM engine starting at state x with |x|>0, using the scaling in Eq. (C.22).

verification.spec: Import the fluid-scaling module and run a stochastic LLM-engine simulation from an initial state x with |x|=1000. Verify that the module produces scaled processes bar B_f^x(t) = B_f(|x|*t)/|x|, bar E^x(t)=E(|x|*t)/|x|, bar F_f^x, bar W_f^x, bar Z_f^x per Eq. (C.22), each returned as a callable/array on [0,T] with correct scaling relationship confirmed by comparing to the unscaled trajectories.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that verifies the SLLN-type limits of Eq. (C.22)-(C.23) on scaled arrival and token-size processes, checking convergence of \bar E^x(t) to λ t and of V_p, V_d scaling to m_p t and m_d t along sequences with |x_k|→∞.

verification.spec: Generate an increasing sequence of initial states |x_k| in {100, 1000, 10000}. For each, simulate the arrival and token-size processes and compute bar E^{x_k}(1). Verify convergence bar E^{x_k}(1) -> lambda as k grows, and analogously that V_p, V_d scaled versions converge to m_p*t and m_d*t at t=1, with error decreasing with |x_k| per Eq. (C.22)-(C.23).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that reproduces Lemma 1: given a sample path in the full-measure set Ω_0 and an unbounded set A⊆X, it extracts a subsequence {x_k}⊆A with |x_k|→∞ for which the fluid-scaled process (\bar B_p^{x_k}(·),\bar B_d^{x_k}(·)) converges uniformly on compact sets to a Lipschitz limit (\hat B_p(·),\hat B_d(·)).

verification.spec: Import the Lemma 1 extraction routine. Given a set A of large initial states with |x_k|->infinity and simulated sample paths, verify that the routine returns a subsequence along which (bar B_p^{x_k}, bar B_d^{x_k}) converges uniformly on [0,T] (sup norm error decreasing to below 0.05 at largest k) to a limit that is Lipschitz continuous with a numerically bounded Lipschitz constant.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that reproduces Lemma 2: from the limit (\hat B_p,\hat B_d) of Lemma 1 and the SLLN limits of Eq. (C.22), it constructs the corresponding limiting functions (\hat F_p,\hat F_d,\hat W_p,\hat W_d,\hat Z_p,\hat Z_d) and verifies uniform-on-compacts convergence along the same subsequence.

verification.spec: Import the Lemma 2 constructor. Given the limit (hat B_p, hat B_d) produced by the Lemma 1 routine and the SLLN limits from Eq. (C.22), verify the module constructs (hat F_p, hat F_d, hat W_p, hat W_d, hat Z_p, hat Z_d) and that along the same subsequence bar F_f^{x_k}, bar W_f^{x_k}, bar Z_f^{x_k} converge uniformly on compact sets to those constructed limits within a numerical tolerance (sup error < 0.05 at largest k).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that reproduces Lemma 3: it verifies that every fluid limit (\hat B,\hat F,\hat W,\hat Z) satisfies all fluid-model equations (C.10)-(C.14), and additionally (C.17) when the underlying scheduling algorithm is work-conserving, thereby confirming it is a (work-conserving) fluid solution.

verification.spec: Import the Lemma 3 verifier. Given a computed fluid limit (hat B, hat F, hat W, hat Z), the verifier must evaluate each of the fluid-model equations (C.10)-(C.14) at multiple times t and return True (residuals below 1e-6). Additionally, when the underlying scheduling algorithm is marked work-conserving, verify equation (C.17) is also satisfied; when it is not work-conserving, verify the checker does NOT enforce (C.17).

sub_tasks.requirements: Using the fluid-limit code, an experiment is run where the LLM engine DTMC is simulated under a work-conserving (K_p,K_d)-FCFS algorithm from large initial states x with |x|→∞ (load condition (C.1) satisfied), and the fluid-scaled \bar Z^x(t) is shown to hit 0 by t≤ f(0)/δ as predicted by Proposition 2(a), confirming numerically that the empirical limit matches a stable fluid solution.

verification.spec: Simulate the LLM-engine DTMC under a work-conserving (K_p,K_d)-FCFS scheduling algorithm with parameters satisfying load condition (C.1) (e.g., lambda=1, m_p=m_d=1, b=4, t_p=1, delta=2). Start from initial states with |x| in {100, 1000, 10000}, compute the fluid-scaled bar Z^x(t) = |Z(|x|*t)|/|x|, and measure the first time T_hit at which bar Z^x(t) reaches 0. Verify T_hit <= f(0)/delta = |x|/(|x|*delta) = 1/delta = 0.5 in the fluid time scale, with tolerance shrinking as |x| grows.

sub_tasks.requirements: Method components (from critique splits and additions)
Code has been implemented such that the arrival process supports iid sequences (a_n, v_p(i), v_d(i), z(i)) with configurable first moments (m_p, m_d) matching Eq. (2.2) of the paper

verification.spec: Instantiate the arrival generator with specified means m_p and m_d and confirm that (i) generated sequences are iid across time slots (chi-square independence test p > 0.01), (ii) sample means converge to configured (m_p, m_d) within 5% over 1e5 samples.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that a batch is valid iff it satisfies the feasibility constraints Eq. (2.5a-d): prefill precedes decode, batched tokens are within unprocessed, at most one decode token per request per batch, and total token load <= token budget b

verification.spec: Construct synthetic states with per-request (p_i, d_i) and call the feasibility validator with hand-crafted batch selections that (a) satisfy all constraints (should be accepted), (b) violate each of (2.5a), (2.5b), (2.5c), (2.5d) individually (should each be rejected). Assert validator returns True/False accordingly.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that batch processing time is modeled as a piecewise-linear function t_{b'} = c + a * max(b' - b_0, 0) of token load b', matching Equation (2.3)

verification.spec: Instantiate the batch-time model with (c, a, b_0). For a grid of b' from 0 to 1024, assert the returned time equals c + a*max(b'-b_0, 0). Verify the function is continuous, piecewise linear, and non-decreasing.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that the feasibility constraints for a scheduling decision pi(x) (Eq. 2.5a-2.5d) are enforced correctly (picture 300x74 encodes the four feasibility constraints)

verification.spec: Implement feasibility checker for pi(x)=(delta_i^p, delta_i^d); verify all four constraints (prefill-before-decode, bounded by unprocessed, sequential decoding <=1 per request per batch, sum <= token budget b) by constructing valid and invalid batches and asserting classifier correctness

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that the post-decision state X'(n) update rule (picture 146x46) is correctly applied: P_i and D_i decrement by delta_i^p and delta_i^d respectively

verification.spec: Apply post-decision update to a synthetic X(n); assert P_i(n)' = P_i(n) - delta_i^p and D_i(n)' = D_i(n) - delta_i^d for all i in Q_n

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that the arrival-update Q_{n+1} = Q'_n union A_n and the state update integrating arrivals (picture 330x29) is correctly applied

verification.spec: Simulate one time slot with arrivals A_n and verify Q_{n+1} equals Q'_n union A_n and that new arrivals have their (v_p, v_d, z) copied into P_i, D_i, Z_i correctly

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that the remaining-processing-time update R(n+1) = max(R(n)-1, 0) + t_{b'} * 1{new batch formed} (picture 149x25) is implemented correctly

verification.spec: Verify the R(n+1) update: when R(n)>0, R decrements by 1 and no batch is formed; when R(n)=0 and a batch of size b' is formed, R(n+1)=t_{b'}

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that a scheduling policy pi is classified as work-conserving iff it forms a full batch b'=b whenever feasible (picture 168x18 supplemental condition)

verification.spec: Given a system state x with enough available tokens to fill budget b, assert pi(x) returns a batch with b' = b; if insufficient tokens exist, assert b' equals total available tokens

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that the Lyapunov function f(X(n)) = sum_{i in Q_n} (t_p * P_i(n) + t_d * D_i(n)) + R(n) (picture 193x27) is computed correctly and exhibits negative drift under work-conserving policies when the load condition holds

verification.spec: Implement the Lyapunov function f; simulate one-step drift E[f(X(n+1)) - f(X(n)) | X(n)=x] for x outside a finite set C under a work-conserving policy at rho<1; assert drift is negative

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that the AI-agent workload diagram (picture 198x163) is instantiated as a network model: orchestrator + load balancer + multiple LLM engines, each with its own scheduler and KV cache

verification.spec: Import the AI-agent network module; assert it contains classes/functions for Orchestrator, LoadBalancer, and LLMEngine (with scheduler and KV cache attributes)

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that the fluid workload Lyapunov function f(t) = sum_j (t_p * Z_p^j(t) + t_d * Z_d^j(t)) (picture 177x25) is computed correctly for the two-type fluid model

verification.spec: Given fluid trajectories (Z_p^j(t), Z_d^j(t)) for j=1,2, compute f(t); verify it equals total remaining workload

Repeat over >=5 randomized states.

verification.spec: Advance the Orca scheduler state to iteration 2 (post iteration 1 of Figure 5) with D, E arrived and holding prefill tokens. Call schedule_iteration(). Assert the returned batch tokens equal exactly {('A','decode'), ('B','decode'), ('C','decode')} as an unordered set, matching Figure 5 Orca row iteration 2.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that the Orca scheduling policy simulator, at Iteration 3 of the Figure 5 workload, returns a mixed batch equal to the multiset {D_p, E_p, B_d, C_d, D_d, E_d} — demonstrating Orca's mixed batching where prefill tokens for D and E are batched together with decode tokens for B, C, D, and E in the same iteration.

Assert the returned batch equals exactly the unordered multiset {('D','prefill'), ('E','prefill'), ('B','decode'), ('C','decode'), ('D','decode'), ('E','decode')}, confirming mixed prefill+decode batching.
